subject.title: ci: add unsigned iOS build workflow

question: Should OpenClaw core own a manually dispatched unsigned iOS `.xcarchive` workflow once the security hardening is fixed?
rationale: The mechanical blockers are repairable, but adding an artifact-producing macOS workflow changes maintainer-owned CI and support surface that automation should not accept silently.

options.title: Harden And Keep The Lane
options.body: Repair the input handling and token hardening, rerun the exact workflow proof, and let maintainers review the resulting unsigned archive lane as core CI.

options.title: Keep It External
options.body: Close or pause this PR and leave the contributor fork workflow as an external experiment until maintainers request core-owned unsigned archive automation.

options.title: Accept Current Risk
options.body: Maintainers could intentionally accept the current dispatch-input and checkout-token risks, but the evidence does not support that as the safe default.

recommendation.title: Harden And Keep The Lane
recommendation.body: Repair the input handling and token hardening, rerun the exact workflow proof, and let maintainers review the resulting unsigned archive lane as core CI.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily CI/security workflow ownership, and Vincent Koc is the strongest current-history match for the relevant workflow hardening patterns.
